cohort: Nulliparas with live-born, singleton gestations ≥37 weeks in spontaneous or induced labor (n=66,539) from the Consortium on Safe Labor database
finding: Cervical dilation on admission and BMI were the two most important risk factors for cesarean delivery in nulliparas.
mod_finding: Cesarean deliveries occurred in 45%, 25%, 14% and 10% of deliveries at <1, 1 to 3, 4 and ≥5 cm dilated, respectively.
